notes: Salary values are cap hits as displayed by the source, not necessarily base salary.
Exact duplicate merged salary/status records are collapsed; source seasons/pages are retained in each merged record.
Team-season snapshots are retained separately so historical page state is not lost.
Expansion-team pages that redirect to another team or season are rejected instead of being duplicated.

mergeHistory.note: Spotrac extension totals/AAV remain separate from Her Hoop Stats yearly salary cap-hit records.

referenceTerms.definition: Active Hardship ContractPlayers that are currently on the roster under a replacement contract due to a hardship or emergency hardship exception.
referenceTerms.details: details Hardship/Replacement contracts are for 75% of the applicable minimum base salary prorated for the time the player is on the roster. Players who only play on replacement contracts do not earn a year of service. Teams may exceed the salary cap to sign a player on a replacement contract under the hardship or emergency hardship exception.

referenceTerms.definition: Contracts that can be signed after the midpoint of the season that last for seven days.
referenceTerms.details: details The contracts are for the applicable minimum base salary prorated for the seven day length of the contract. The contracts are not guaranteed even though they are signed after the midpoint of the season. Players who only play on seven-day contracts do not earn a year of service.

referenceTerms.definition: Waived players that have agreed to receive a buyout that is less than their full protected salary in exchange for being waived by their team.
referenceTerms.details: details A player may choose to do this so they can play for another team for the remainder of the season.

referenceTerms.definition: Complete Hardship ContractPlayers that were on the roster under a replacement contract due to a hardship or emergency hardship exception.
referenceTerms.details: details Hardship/Replacement contracts are for 75% of the applicable minimum base salary prorated for the time the player is on the roster. Players who only play on replacement contracts do not earn a year of service.

referenceTerms.definition: Contracts that can be signed after the midpoint of the season that last for seven days.
referenceTerms.details: details The contracts are for the applicable minimum base salary prorated for the seven day length of the contract. The contracts are not guaranteed even though they are signed after the midpoint of the season. Players who only play on seven-day contracts do not earn a year of service.

referenceTerms.definition: An out of contract player who had a core qualifying offer extended from their current team.
referenceTerms.details: details Cored players may not negotiate or sign with another team, but they may help facilitate a sign-and-trade agreement with their current desired future team. A core qualifying offer must be a one-year supermaximum contract. After the core offer has been made, the team and player may negotiate any contract they mutually agree to.

referenceTerms.definition: Future veteran contract salaries that are guaranteed to the player if they are cut due to lack of skill, injury or illness, with the amount determined by a percentage of the salary cap.
referenceTerms.details: details Teams may have up to six veteran contracts that are protected.

referenceTerms.definition: Players who have been suspended for the remainder of the season voluntarily, as a result of a hold-out, or due to a non-WNBA basketball injury.
referenceTerms.details: details These players' salaries do not count on the cap, they are not paid, and they do not take up a roster spot.

referenceTerms.definition: The maximum base player salary that can be offered to players by a team under standard circumstances.
The maximum base player salary that can be offered to players by a team in exceptional circumstances that is higher than the standard maximum.
referenceTerms.details: details Players primarily become eligible for a supermax contract if they are signing a rookie extension or have at least five years of service and sign with their current team.

referenceTerms.definition: Players who are temporarily unavailable to play due to pregnancy or recent childbirth.
referenceTerms.details: details These players receive a pregnancy disability benefit of 100% of base salary for the remainder of contract while out due to pregnancy or childbirth. Their salaries still count on the cap but they don't count as a roster spot while unavailable.

referenceTerms.definition: Starting in 2026, the first year of a lottery pick’s contract is fully guaranteed. For all rookie-scale contracts since 2020, the fourth year has a team option that is fully guaranteed if the option is exercised.
referenceTerms.details: details Protected Rookie Scale contracts do not count against the limit for protected veterans.

referenceTerms.definition: Veteran contract salaries that are guaranteed to the player if they are cut due to lack of skill, injury or illness.
referenceTerms.details: details Teams may have up to six veteran contracts that are protected.

referenceTerms.definition: An out of contract player eligible only for the reserved player designation who has received a reserved qualifying offer from their current team.
referenceTerms.details: details A reserved player is free to negotiate a contract with their own team with different terms from the qualifying offer, but they may not negotiate with any other WNBA teams.

referenceTerms.definition: An out of contract player eligible for restricted free agency but not unrestricted free agency who had a restricted qualifying offer extended from their current team.
referenceTerms.details: details The player may sign an offer sheet with another team, but the prior team has the "right of first refusal" to match the terms. If the prior team decides to match, the player remains with the prior team under the offer sheet terms. If not, they play for the new team under the offer sheet terms.

referenceTerms.definition: An out of contract player who opted out or was suspended for the final season of their contract; these players do not become free agents.
referenceTerms.details: details Suspended-Contract Expired players are free to negotiate a contract with their own team but they may not negotiate with any other WNBA teams.

referenceTerms.definition: A team has the option to retain a drafted player on a rookie scale contract for a fourth year at the salary specified in the CBA.
referenceTerms.details: details The option must be exercised by May 15 following the player's second contract year. If the option is not exercised, the player becomes an Unrestricted Free Agent after their third contract year.

referenceTerms.definition: Players that have been suspended for less than the full season or for indefinite injuries that don't result from basketball.
referenceTerms.details: details These players' salaries still count on their team's salary cap, but they are not paid and don't count as a roster spot while they are suspended.

referenceTerms.definition: Contracts that are signed without any base salary protection.
referenceTerms.details: details These players may be cut and are only owed the prorated amount of their salary for the time the player was on the regular season roster. However, their contracts become fully guaranteed for the year after the midpoint of the season.

referenceTerms.definition: An out of contract player that is free to negotiate with any team in the WNBA.
Players with contracts that have been cut from the team and were not picked up on waivers by another team.
referenceTerms.details: details These players are owed the full amount they are paid or to be paid by the team that waived them, but do not count as a roster spot.

referenceTerms.definition: The number of years a player is on the active roster for at least one day of the regular season.
referenceTerms.details: details Exceptions are detailed in the WNBA CBA FAQ.
